attributes.body_ja:
「ものの」は、(A) が事実（じじつ）であることを認（みと）めつつ、(B) という結果（けっか）や状況（じょうきょう）は (A) が原因（げんいん）ではない、 (A) からは予測（よそく）できない、また (A) と正反対（せいはんたい）であることを表（あらわ）す硬（かたい）い接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）です。

「ものの」は動詞（どうし）、イ形容詞（けいようし）、「である」を伴（ともな）う名詞（めいし）、「な」を伴（ともな）うナ形容詞（けいようし）の後（あと）に直接（ちょくせつ）付（つ）きます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「ものの」は前後（ぜんご）の文（ぶん）で主語（しゅご）や話題（わだい）が同（おな）じ場合（ばあい）にのみ使（つか）うことができます。
attributes.body:
ものの is a formal conjunction-particle used to illustrate that while (A) is a fact, the result or condition of (B) cannot be attributed to (A), could not be predicted through (A), or is in direct contrast to (A).

ものの may appear directly after verb, い-Adjectives, nouns followed by である, or な-Adjectives followed by な.

Caution

ものの may only be used when the subject or topic of the sentence is the same in both the statements preceding and following it.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese
新完全マスター文法 N2

attributes.description: 接続・意味・使い方・例文

attributes.body: ものを and ものの are similar in that both can express contrast (i.e. 'although'), but ものを specifically contrasts something that was expected to happen with what actually happened because the action was not done, e.g. みんなで協力すればいいものを ('although it would have been good if you had all cooperated'), while ものの can be used for general contrasts 毎朝走っているものの、足はあまり速くない ('Although I run every morning, I'm not that fast.'). Additionally, ものを will most often come at the end of a sentence, while ものの will be followed by the reason or unexpected result.

first_relatable.title: ものを
first_relatable.meaning: But, Although, If only, I wish I had

attributes.body: ものの expresses contrast, similar to 'although' in English, showing that while one thing is true, another contradicts it. が also expresses contrast, but its nuance is weaker, and in some cases, it merely introduces a statement without implying contrast. が is more general, while ものの is more specific. Both are formal and more common in writing than in casual speech.

Both ものの and けれども can appear at the end of a clause to show contrast. けれども (or the casual けど) usually expresses a simple contrast or adds background information, and is used in a wide range of situations. In contrast, ものの has the specific nuance of 'While A is true, B is not,' and is less colloquial, more commonly found in writing or formal speech.

Both express concession but differ in tone. にもかかわらず is formal and often used in writing to highlight strong contrast or surprise, as in 雨にもかかわらず試合が行われた (The game was held despite the rain). ものの is less formal and means even though or but, as in 雨が降ったものの試合は行われた (It rained, but the game was held).

first_relatable.title: にもかかわらず
first_relatable.meaning: Despite, In spite of, Regardless, Nevertheless

attributes.body: Both express contrast between expectation and reality. つつ(も) implies that an action continues over time while another, opposing reality exists, as in 危険だと知りつつも挑戦した (I knew it was dangerous, yet I tried). ものの simply means although/even though, without emphasizing continuation, as in 雨は降ったものの試合は行われた (It rained, but the game was held).

first_relatable.title: つつ(も)
first_relatable.meaning: Even while ~ing, Even though ~ing, Despite ~ing, Although ~ing

attributes.body: のに and ものの both express contrast, but differ in nuance and tone. のに is more casual and often conveys disappointment or regret. It can also end a sentence to imply 'If only (A)!'. ものの is more formal and means 'although (A), (B) didn't follow as expected,' often with an implicit contrast. Unlike のに, it is not generally used alone at the end of a sentence..

Both ものの and 割に express contrast, but in different ways. ものの links two opposing facts to mean 'despite', e.g. '話せるものの、字は読めない' ('Despite the fact that he can speak, he can't read characters'). 割に describes a quality being out of proportion with something else, e.g. '高い割にはあまり美味しくない' ('For being expensive, it's not very tasty').

second_relatable.title: 割に
second_relatable.meaning: Although, Despite, Rather...for, Unexpectedly, Comparatively, Considering
